assessments.reasoning: The dated W3C announcement names XPath 3.1 as one of six distinct published W3C Recommendations and links to the normative edition. The independently downloaded full response SHA-256 matches the registered source revision. The announcement identifies XPath as an expression language and gives distinct entries and descriptions for XQuery and XDM. XPath and XQuery are related through named technologies with separately identified language and data-model specifications. The dated W3C documentation and language identity facet match. The scope is the 3.1 Recommendation series distinctions. The governing Recommendation describes host integration. With separate language and host roles, integration with XQuery or XSLT leaves the documented XPath boundary intact.
